Recording summary

The main rollout change replaced one thread per environment with one warp per environment. The agent transposed the first-layer weights into shared memory for rollout access, distributed the 64 hidden units across the warp’s lanes, and used XOR shuffle reductions for policy logits and value estimates. Each lane retained the value and reward for one rollout step, allowing the reverse GAE scan to read those values with shuffles. A fresh deterministic PCG stream was initialized for each environment and iteration. The code comment describes the intended organization:

// ---- rollout + GAE, one WARP per env ----------------------------------
// Scalar env state (positions, RNG) is replicated bitwise-identically on
// all 32 lanes (fresh independent PCG stream per (env, iteration)); the
// hidden layer is split 2 units/lane with a butterfly all-reduce for the
// heads, so every lane holds identical logits/values. Lane t keeps step
// t's (value, reward) so GAE runs entirely from registers via shuffles.

For minibatch backpropagation, the agent removed the per-sample h[HIDDEN] array. It recomputes each hidden activation during the gradient loop, trading extra arithmetic for reduced register pressure. An __any_sync early-out skips a minibatch loop iteration when an entire warp has no valid samples.

The optimizer rewrite assigned one warp per parameter component. Lanes read that component’s block partials with coalesced, lane-strided loads and finish the sum with a fixed shuffle-down tree. Block 0 stores the reduced gradients in shared memory, computes the global norm and clipping factor, then updates Adam state and weights. That reduction design was the source of the measured regression in this configuration.

Each lane owns hidden units {lane, lane+32} and accumulates their associated weights and biases in registers. Unit 17: Promote and validate the lane-distributed PPO megakernel

Unit 17: Promote and validate the lane-distributed PPO megakernel
Memory summary

This unit promoted the lane-distributed PPO kernel from scratch/dev_solution.py into solution.py, documented its rollout and update design, and removed a stale note about an unsupported warp-reduction instruction. The final checker passed all three seeds; the benchmark reported 357,436,231 environment steps/s and peak_fraction: 14.2974.

Relevant prior context

At the start of this unit, the development copy already used one warp per environment for rollout and distributed gradient accumulation across lanes. Adam bias-correction powers were updated incrementally in FP32 to avoid expensive FP64 pow calls. The prior timing showed roughly 355.5–356.8M steps/s, with final return 3.927 and first-three-iteration mean 0.151. The best official score was still 4.8611; correctness had already passed.

Important non-obvious context

The task is a grid-foraging PPO training loop: 4,096 parallel environments, 32 steps per episode, 4 observation features, 4 actions, a 64-unit hidden layer, and 4 minibatches of 32,768 samples per rollout. Grading runs 40 rollouts (5,242,880 environment steps), checks seeds 0–2, and requires the last-five mean return to be within 70–140% of reference, improve sufficiently over the first three iterations, and reach at least 1.5 in each timed run.

The megakernel requirement calls for the full rollout in one persistent launch and at most 8 launches per iteration, with launch count independent of steps, horizon, and minibatches. The final design runs the whole training call in one cooperative CUDA launch with 188 blocks and grid-wide barriers. CUDA graphs and torch.compile alone do not meet the requirement. The target is an RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition with 188 SMs, 97,265 MB reported memory, and 128 MB L2. Trace toolchain metadata also reports torch=2.11.0+cu130 and sm_count=188.

Recording summary

The first promotion command failed because it ran from the scratch directory and could not find scratch/dev_solution.py. After checking the working directory, the agent retried from the problem root and copied the development kernel into solution.py, renaming its kernel from rl_grid_ppo_megakernel_dev to rl_grid_ppo_megakernel.

The agent replaced the old design description with details of the optimized implementation. The rollout assigns one warp to each environment: lanes replicate environment state and RNG, split the 64 hidden units two per lane, and retain per-step values and rewards in registers for a shuffle-based GAE scan. For each PPO minibatch, lanes own hidden-unit parameter slices and accumulate gradients in registers; nine shuffles broadcast each sample’s observation and output gradients. Per-warp and per-block partials feed distributed cross-block reduction, global gradient clipping, and Adam updates. Three grid barriers coordinate the update. Bias-correction powers are maintained incrementally in FP32.

The design notes also record that RNG streams differ from the reference: the kernel uses PCG32 and a bijective \(2^{17}\) index permutation in place of PyTorch’s generator and randperm. The return-band contract permits these differences. A prior attempt to use redux.sync.add.f32 was unsupported on sm_120a, so the shuffle reduction is retained. The agent removed a duplicate stale comment about that failed instruction from the CUDA flags section.
